column8: Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3c, the card's best: Osaka presumed every bill backed and tested it only after its date, which served a holder who could wait for the magistrate; co-sponsors file her figure as committed (four of four, 16 Nov) and plan around it from 2031, so she states only what she owns (IPS l.15); sharpens Q170-014 (the court as a presumption), carries rows 14-15, one outside name per part against Q170-010; committed, never secured.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3d with row 1: backed and empty bills looked alike, so no market could police them; qualifies Q170-010 (the two kinds existed but could not be told apart); her side is visible, since the funds publish holdings daily (Q26-021) and she can show the credit (Q157-043); carries row 13.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 with row 1, the dated hinge: in 1771 the test moved from rice held to delivery failing on its date; say Osaka tested a bill only on and after its date, never that Osaka supplied ink's second half (row 24); a policy trade that eased lords' borrowing.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q170-014 (the 1761 ban and its failure): adds only the ban's text and stated reason (harm to trade in other bills); the link to SD-3 (Q150-019) is a stretch, since first money is about order, not taint.

Thu 19 Nov: store, with rows 21-22 only, as the overbooking bet in Osaka's form (trusting holders left bills unclaimed, so a sure warehouse held rice for 30% of them); a second over-issue ratio beside Q170-011, never both; outcome unrecorded, the silver figure conflicts and stays out.

Thu 19 Nov: store; breaks under its own column: reputation polices a repeat issuer and Laura is one (a stated figure unpaid costs her credibility with co-sponsors, card Q109), so the point is only that her figure does not lean on reputation; Mori and Ito read through Takatsuki.

Thu 19 Nov: store beside IPS l.9: issuers write paper beyond their stock when their income falls, the history behind pledges weakening in the downturn her kept half answers (IPS l.15); say co-sponsors' budgets can fall in the same downturn, never fall together (Q50); Takatsuki's narrative, no quote.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store, pedigree for IPS l.11 (no payment on anybody else's money): the money-dealers refused a backstop too small to pay (1,000 against about 40,000 kan, 2.5%, Keel arithmetic checks) and warned it would invite more paper; textbook moral hazard in 1772 words, from slides summarising the diary; part of the evidence correcting Q170-013.

Thu 19 Nov: corrects Q170-013: the 1773 buyback was declared, Takatsuki finds no record that public silver was paid, and it was dropped in 1782; so Q170-013's made good only by a sovereign guarantee, its prediction of the plan's issuer and idea 3's packaging of Q170-010, Q170-011 and Q170-013 (best three, item 1) are withdrawn; the facts of Q170-010 and Q170-011 stand; a guard, with one small pencil fact.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q58-026 (backing sworn, not shown): Chikugo's definitely not empty rice is the same issuer assurance a holder cannot check; one merchant's record of one run.

Thu 19 Nov: CONFLICTING, rated on what is verified: Schaede p. 495 (checked at source today) says the government paid out the claims and probably gave this guaranty, p. 511 that it began guaranteeing all rice bills in 1773; Takatsuki's archival reading finds the buyback declared and never shown paid; the guard on Q170-013 holds either way (never made safe by a government guarantee); fix its wording: declared in 1773, dropped in 1782, no record of payment, never never funded as a flat fact.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d or Table 1's reason, the sharpest break: Osaka's one check of the rice held (Goto's seal, 1783-87) ended when the domains shut their doors, while her funds publish holdings daily by rule (Q26-021) and Table 1 lists every bond (Q58-026), so her check needs no one's consent; the resistance is Takatsuki's inference; never her two Treasury funds (idea 1's wording: she holds five iBond funds and the top rests on one, IBTM).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q178-002: the same unseen stock, from a slide's summary.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q178-001: the contemporary witness that lenders trusted the court's strict handling, not the warehouse; if Osaka's court is used this is its one voice; one merchant's view.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q178-001: the court that never refused debt suits, read in a dissertation summary only; same point.

Thu 19 Nov: store guard beside Q170-017: if Dojima's 1730 licence is named, the trust came from the 1732 court, not the licence (price support meant to be temporary); the 1732 detail rests on a book review.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c reserve, one clause at most: figures match NUMBERS 3 ($117,731 at zero interest, $589 margin, $2,142 rounding, room $2,731); breaks under its own column, since a fire is sudden while the margin covers slow costs (about 0.27%), and an early end at zero interest leaves the top $4,589 short; second-hand (Miyamoto unread); fund costs beyond the fee explain the margin more plainly.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the rule behind row 17 (checked at source today: the issuer remains in charge of storage only): a fund's owner carries its costs, about 0.27% beyond the fees (NUMBERS 0), and the margin keeps them off co-sponsors; the $4,589 early-end case breaks it.
Thu 19 Nov: CONFLICTING, store guard only: two historians read monk bills differently; never monk bill in the report.

Thu 19 Nov: CONFLICTING, store guard: 1652 in Schaede against 1744 in Takatsuki for the first shogunal ban; say banned more than once; also qualifies parent idea 3's list of bans (1650s, 1660, 1761), not a parent row.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d's reserves, aha for a reader outside finance: paper is oversold only when not every holder claims, and every holder of her top claims it in full, so only the kept half, promised to no one, holds shares (IPS l.15); fix: overselling is lawful and the bumped are paid cash on the day, never lawful because of the cash (DOT's own page unread); sits beside H6-049, competes with SD-3 (Q150-019) for 3d's one outside name.

Thu 19 Nov: store, the figure behind row 21 if used: 0.15 involuntary bumps in 10,000 and about 3.2 in all (Keel arithmetic checks: 3,376 and 74,374 of 231.7 million); one quarter of one industry, decoration alone.

Thu 19 Nov: store or 3c's dating clause: modern warehouse law also holds the issuer to an empty receipt unless its face says it does not know (said to contain); fix: say modern law reached the same rule, never kept Osaka's; the link to 3c's dated range is Keel's, and the range before the move is no receipt; never the law draws the same line as pencil and ink (Q157-042).

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, rival to Q186-010 (accounting's two tests) for the one clause on ink's two halves; fix: Osaka's court enforced a bill after its date, the owed side of Q170-014, so never Osaka gave ink's pays on its date half; keep only that neither alone is ink and that Laura makes the owned check herself before she speaks.
